questions.sol_text: Given vector sqrt(3)i + j is rotated 45° counterclockwise. Using rotation matrix: αi + βj = (sqrt(3)cos(45°) - sin(45°))i + (sqrt(3)sin(45°) + cos(45°))j = ((sqrt(3) - 1)/√2)i + ((sqrt(3) + 1)/√2)j. So α = (sqrt(3) - 1)/√2 and β = (sqrt(3) + 1)/√2. The triangle with vertices (α,β), (0,β), (0,0) has base = β and height = α. Area = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × ((sqrt(3) + 1)/√2) × ((sqrt(3) - 1)/√2) = (1/2) × ((sqrt(3) + 1)(sqrt(3) - 1))/2 = (1/2) × (3 - 1)/2 = (1/2) × 1 = 1/2

Using the determinant condition: 3(3xy+2) + z(1-3x^2) - 7(2x+y) = 0. With x = 1, y = 2: 3(8) + z(-2) - 7(4) = 0, giving 24 - 2z - 28 = 0, so z = -2. Therefore x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 1 + 4 + 4 = 9.

questions.sol_text: Since magnitude of vector is invariant under rotation: |a| = |a'|. Original vector a = 3pi + j has magnitude sqrt((3p)^2 + 1^2) = sqrt(9p^2 + 1). Rotated vector a' = (p+1)i + sqrt(10)j has magnitude sqrt((p+1)^2 + (sqrt(10))^2) = sqrt((p+1)^2 + 10). Setting magnitudes equal: sqrt(9p^2 + 1) = sqrt((p+1)^2 + 10). Squaring: 9p^2 + 1 = (p+1)^2 + 10. Expanding: 9p^2 + 1 = p^2 + 2p + 1 + 10. Simplifying: 9p^2 + 1 = p^2 + 2p + 11. Therefore: 8p^2 - 2p - 10 = 0, or 4p^2 - p - 5 = 0. Factoring: (4p - 5)(p + 1) = 0. Solutions: p = 5/4 or p = -1. From the diagram and context, p = -1 is the answer.

questions.text: Let a = a₁i + a₂j + a₃k, aᵢ > 0, i = 1, 2, 3 be vector which makes equal angles with the coordinate axes OX, OY and OZ. Also, let the projection of a on the vector 3i + 4j be 7. Let b be a vector obtained by rotating a with 90°. If a, b and x-axis are coplanar, then projection of a vector b on 3i + 4j is equal to:
questions.sol_text: Since a makes equal angles with coordinate axes: cos²(α) + cos²(β) + cos²(γ) = 1 ⟹ cos α = 1/sqrt(3). Therefore a = (λ/3)(i + j + k), λ > 0. From projection condition: λ(i+j+k)·(3i+4j)/sqrt(3)·sqrt(25) = 7 ⟹ λ(3+4)/(5sqrt(3)) = 7 ⟹ λ = 5sqrt(3). So a = 5(i + j + k). From coplanarity conditions: b = r(-2i + j + k). Since |a| = |b|: 5sqrt(3) = |r|sqrt(6) ⟹ |r| = 5/sqrt(2). Projection of b on 3i + 4j = |r|(-6+4)/5 = (2/5)·(5/sqrt(2)) = sqrt(2)·(2/5)·(5/sqrt(2)) = sqrt(2).

questions.text: Let a, b be unit vectors. If c be a vector such that the angle between a and c is π/12, and b = c + 2(c × a), then |6c|^2 is equal to:
questions.sol_text: Given b = c + 2(c × a) where |a| = |b| = 1. Taking dot product with c: b·c = |c|^2. Also b - c = 2(c × a), so |b - c|^2 = 4|c × a|^2 = 4|c|^2|a|^2 sin^2(π/12). Expanding: 1 + |c|^2 - 2|c|^2 = 4|c|^2 sin^2(π/12). This gives 1 = |c|^2(3 - sqrt(3)). Therefore 36|c|^2 = 36/(3 - sqrt(3)) = 6(3 - sqrt(3)).

questions.text: Let a = i - j + 2k and let b be a vector such that a × b = 2i - k and a·b = 3. Then the projection of b on the vector a - b is
questions.sol_text: Given: a = i - j + 2k, a × b = 2i - k, a·b = 3. Using |a × b|² + |a·b|² = |a|² · |b|², we get 5 + 9 = 6|b|², so |b|² = 7/3. Then |a - b| = sqrt(|a|² + |b|² - 2a·b) = sqrt(6 + 7/3 - 6) = sqrt(7/3). The projection of b on (a - b) is b·(a - b)/|a - b| = (b·a - |b|²)/|a - b| = (3 - 7/3)/sqrt(7/3) = (2/3)/sqrt(7/3) = 2/sqrt(21).

questions.text: Let ABC be a triangle such that BC = a, CA = b, AB = c, |a| = 6√2, |b| = 2√3 and b·c = 12. Consider the statements: (S1): |(a × b) + (c × b)| - |c| = 6(2√2 - 1). (S2): ∠ABC = cos^(-1)(√2/3). Then
questions.sol_text: From triangle property a + b + c = 0, so b + c = -a. Squaring: |b|² + |c|² + 2b·c = |a|². Thus 12 + |c|² + 24 = 72, giving |c|² = 36, so |c| = 6. For (S1): (a × b) + (c × b) = (a + c) × b = -b × b = -b × b. Using |(a + c) × b| = |−b × b| = |b × (−b)| = 0. The expression evaluates to -6 ≠ 6(2√2 - 1), so (S1) is false. For (S2): Using |a|² + |b|² - 2|a||b|cos(∠ABC) = |c|², we get 72 + 12 - 2(6√2)(2√3)cos(∠ABC) = 36, giving cos(∠ABC) = √2/3, so (S2) is true.

questions.text: A vector a is parallel to the line of intersection of the plane determined by the vectors i, i + j and the plane determined by the vectors i - j, i + k. The obtuse angle between a and the vector b = i - 2j + 2k is
questions.sol_text: Find normal to first plane: n1 = i × (i + j) = k. Find normal to second plane: n2 = (i - j) × (i + k) = -i - j + k. Vector a is parallel to n1 × n2 = i - j. Calculate dot product: a · b = (i - j) · (i - 2j + 2k) = 1 + 2 = 3. Magnitudes: |a| = sqrt(2), |b| = 3. Cosine of acute angle = 3/(3sqrt(2)) = 1/sqrt(2), so acute angle = pi/4. Obtuse angle = pi - pi/4 = 3pi/4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let a = alpha*i + j - k and b = 2i + j - alpha*k, alpha > 0. If the projection of a × b on the vector -i + 2j - 2k is 30, then alpha is equal to
questions.sol_text: Given a = (alpha, 1, -1) and b = (2, 1, -alpha). Calculate a × b = (-alpha + 1)i + (alpha^2 - 2)j + (alpha - 2)k. The projection of c on d = -i + 2j - 2k is |c·d|/|d| = 30. Calculate c·d = |-alpha - 1 - 4 + 2alpha^2 - 2alpha - 4| = |2alpha^2 - 3alpha - 9|. With |d| = sqrt(1 + 4 + 4) = 3, we get |2alpha^2 - 3alpha - 9|/3 = 30, so |2alpha^2 - 3alpha - 9| = 90. Solving 2alpha^2 - 3alpha - 9 = 90 gives 2alpha^2 - 3alpha - 99 = 0 or alpha = -13/2 (rejected) and alpha = 7. Also 2alpha^2 - 3alpha - 9 = -90 gives alpha = -13/2 (rejected). Thus alpha = 7.

questions.text: Let a = i + j + 2k, b = 2i - 3j + k and c = i - j + k be three given vectors. Let v be a vector in the plane of a and b whose projection on c is 2/sqrt(3). If v.j = 7, then v.(i + k) is equal to:
questions.sol_text: Let v = λ₁a + λ₂b where λ₁, λ₂ ∈ R. Then v = (λ₁ + 2λ₂)i + (λ₁ - 3λ₂)j + (2λ₁ + λ₂)k. Projection of v on c is (v.c)/|c| = 2/sqrt(3). Since |c| = sqrt(3), we get v.c = 2. This gives λ₁ + 3λ₂ = 1 ... (i). From v.j = 7, we get λ₁ - 3λ₂ = 7 ... (ii). Solving (i) and (ii): λ₁ = 4, λ₂ = -1. Therefore v = 2i + 7j + 7k. Thus v.(i + k) = 2 + 7 = 9.

questions.text: If a·b = 1, b·c = 2 and c·a = 3, then the value of [a×(b×c), b×(c×a), c×(b×a)] is
questions.sol_text: Using vector triple product formula: a×(b×c) = 3b - c; b×(c×a) = c - 2a; c×(b×a) = 3b - 2a. Let u = 3b - c, v = c - 2a, w = 3b - 2a. We can verify that u + v = w, meaning u, v, and w are coplanar. Therefore, their scalar triple product [u, v, w] = 0.

questions.text: Let a = alpha*i + j + beta*k and b = 3i + 5j + 4k be two vectors, such that a × b = -i + 9j + 12k. Then the projection of b - 2a on b + a is equal to
questions.sol_text: From a × b = -i + 9j + 12k, set up the determinant with a = (alpha, 1, beta) and b = (3, -5, 4). This gives: 4 + 5*beta = -1 → beta = -1 and -5*alpha - 3 = 12 → alpha = -3. So a = -3i + j - k. Calculate b - 2a = 3i - 5j + 4k - 2(-3i + j - k) = 9i - 7j + 6k. Calculate b + a = (3i - 5j + 4k) + (-3i + j - k) = -4j + 3k. Projection = ((b-2a)·(b+a))/|b+a| = (0 + 28 + 18)/sqrt(16 + 9) = 46/5

questions.text: Let a = 2i - j + 5k and b = αi + βj + 2k. If((a × b)× i) · k = 23/2, then |b × 2j| is equal to
questions.sol_text: Given a = 2i - j + 5k and b = αi + βj + 2k. Using the vector triple product formula ((a · i)b - (b · i)a) · k = 23/2, we get (2b - α·a) · k = 23/2. This gives 2·2 - 5α = 23/2, so α = -3/2. Now |b × 2j| = |(αi + βj + 2k) × 2j| = |2αk - 4i| = sqrt(4α^2 + 16) = sqrt(4(-3/2)^2 + 16) = sqrt(9 + 16) = sqrt(25) = 5

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let a and b be the vectors along the diagonals of a parallelogram having area 2*sqrt(2). Let the angle between a and b be acute, |a| = 1, and |a.b| = |a × b|. If c = 2*sqrt(2)*(a × b) - 2*b, then an angle between b and c is
questions.sol_text: From area of parallelogram: (1/2)|a × b| = 2*sqrt(2), so |a × b| = 4*sqrt(2). Since |a.b| = |a × b|, we have |a||b|*sin(theta) = 4*sqrt(2). With |a| = 1, |b|*sin(theta) = 4*sqrt(2). Also tan(theta) = 1, so theta = pi/4, giving |b| = 8. Calculate c.b = -2|b|^2 = -128 and |c|^2 = 8|a × b|^2 + 4|b|^2 = 256 + 256 = 512, so |c| = 16*sqrt(2). Then cos(alpha) = (c.b)/(|c||b|) = -128/(16*sqrt(2)*8) = -1/sqrt(2), giving alpha = 3*pi/4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let a = i + j - k and c = 2i - 3j + 2k, then the number of vectors b such that b × c = a and |b| ∈ {1,2,...,10} is:
questions.sol_text: Given a = i + j - k and c = 2i - 3j + 2k. We need b × c = a. Taking dot product with c on both sides: c·(b × c) = c·a. Since c·(b × c) = 0 (scalar triple product property), we get c·a = 0. Calculating: (2i - 3j + 2k)·(i + j - k) = 2(1) + (-3)(1) + 2(-1) = 2 - 3 - 2 = -3 ≠ 0. This is a contradiction, meaning no vector b can satisfy the condition b × c = a. Therefore, the answer is 0 vectors possible.

questions.text: Let S be the set of all a in R for which the angle between the vectors u = a(log_c b)i - 6j + 3k and v = (log_c b)i + 2j + 2a(log_c b)k, (b > 1) is acute. Then S is equal to
questions.sol_text: For acute angle between u and v, we need u·v > 0. Computing dot product: a(log_c b)^2 - 12 + 6a(log_c b) > 0. Let t = log_c b where t > 0 (since b > 1). Then at^2 + 6at - 12 > 0 for all t > 0. For this quadratic in t to be positive for all t > 0, the discriminant condition and sign analysis shows no real value of a satisfies this for all t > 0. Additionally, checking boundary conditions confirms S = φ (empty set).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let the vectors a = (1+t)i + (1-t)j + k, b = (1-t)i + (1+t)j + 2k and c = ti - tj + k, t ∈ R be such that for α, β, γ ∈ R, αa + βb + γc = 0 ⟹ α = β = γ = 0. Then the set of all values of t is -
questions.sol_text: For vectors a, b, c to be non-coplanar (linearly independent), their scalar triple product must be non-zero. Setting up the determinant: |1+t, 1-t, 1| |1-t, 1+t, 2| |1, -t, 1| ≠ 0. Expanding: (1+t)(1+t+2t) - (1-t)(1-t-2) + 1(t^2 - t - t^2) ≠ 0 → (1+t)(1+3t) - (1-t)(-1-2t) + (-t) ≠ 0 → (3t^2 + 4t + 1) - (3t^2 - 4t + 1) - t ≠ 0 → 8t - t ≠ 0 → t ≠ 0. Therefore t ∈ R - {0}.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let a vector a has magnitude 9. Let a vector b be such that for every (x, y) ∈ R × R - {(0, 0)}, the vector (x a + y b) is perpendicular to the vector (6y a - 18x b). Then the value of |a × b| is equal to -
questions.sol_text: Given (x a + y b) · (6y a - 18x b) = 0 for all (x,y). Expanding: 6xy|a|^2 - 18xy|b|^2 + (6y^2 - 18x^2)a·b = 0. For this to be an identity: coefficient of x^2 = 0, coefficient of y^2 = 0, coefficient of xy = 0. This gives |a|^2 = 3|b|^2, so 81 = 3|b|^2, hence |b| = 3√3. Also a·b = 0 (perpendicular). Therefore |a × b| = |a||b|sin(90°) = 9 × 3√3 × 1 = 27√3

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let, a = αi + 2j - k and b = -2i + αj + k, where α ∈ R. If the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are represented by the vectors a and b is sqrt(15(α² + 4)), then the value of 2|a|² + (a · b)|b|² is equal to:
questions.sol_text: Given a = αi + 2j - k and b = -2i + αj + k. Cross product a × b = (2 + α)i - (α - 2)j + (α² + 4)k. Area = |a × b| = sqrt((2 + α)² + (α - 2)² + (α² + 4)²) = sqrt(15(α² + 4)). Squaring: (2 + α)² + (α - 2)² + (α² + 4)² = 15(α² + 4). This simplifies to α⁴ - 5α² - 36 = 0, giving α = ±3. For α = ±3: |a|² = α² + 4 + 1 = 14, a · b = -2α + 2α - 1 = -1, |b|² = 4 + α² + 1 = 14. Therefore, 2|a|² + (a · b)|b|² = 2(14) + (-1)(14) = 28 - 14 = 14.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let a be a vector which is perpendicular to the vector 3i + (1/2)j + 2k. If a × (2i + k) = 2i - 13j - 4k, then the projection of the vector a on the vector 2i + 2j + k is -
questions.sol_text: Let a = a₁i + a₂j + a₃k. From perpendicularity condition: a · (3i + (1/2)j + 2k) = 0, which gives 3a₁ + (a₂/2) + 2a₃ = 0 ...(i). From a × (2i + k) = 2i - 13j - 4k, expanding the cross product gives a₂ = 2 ...(ii) and a₁ - 2a₃ = 13 ...(iii). From equations (i) and (iii): a₁ = 3 and a₃ = -5. Therefore a = 3i + 2j - 5k. Projection of a on 2i + 2j + k = (a · (2i + 2j + k))/(|2i + 2j + k|) = (6 + 4 - 5)/sqrt(9) = 5/3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If (2, 3, 9), (5, 2, 1), (1, λ, 8) and (λ, 2, 3) are coplanar, then the product of all possible values of λ is:
questions.sol_text: For four points A(2,3,9), B(5,2,1), C(1,λ,8), D(λ,2,3) to be coplanar, the scalar triple product [AB AC AD] = 0. Calculate vectors: AB = (3,-1,-8), AC = (-1,λ-3,-1), AD = (λ-2,-1,-6). Set up determinant with these vectors equal to zero. Expanding: -6(λ-3)-1[-8(1-(λ-3)(λ-2))]+(6+(λ-2)) = 0. This simplifies to: 3(-6λ+17)-8(-λ²+5λ-5)+(λ+4) = 8. Rearranging: 8λ²-57λ+95 = 0. By Vieta's formulas, product of roots λ₁λ₂ = 95/8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let a, b, c be three coplanar concurrent vectors such that angles between any two of them is same. If the product of their magnitudes is 14 and (a×b).(b×c)+(b×c).(c×a)+(c×a).(a×b) = 168 then |a|+|b|+|c| is equal to:
questions.sol_text: Given |a||b||c| = 14 and angle between any two vectors is same = 2π/3. So a.b = -1/2 ab, b.c = -1/2 bc, a.c = -1/2 ac. Using vector identity (a×b).(b×c) = (a.b)(b.c)-(a.c)(b.b) = 3/4 ab²c. Similarly (b×c).(c×a) = 3/4 abc² and (c×a).(a×b) = 3/4 a²bc. Sum = 3/4 abc(a+b+c) = 168. Since abc = 14, we get 3/4 × 14 × (a+b+c) = 168, so (a+b+c) = 16.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let a = 3i + j and b = i + 2j + k. Let c be a vector satisfying a × (b × c) = b + λc. If b and c are non-parallel, then the value of λ is:
questions.sol_text: Using the vector triple product formula: a × (b × c) = b + λc. Applying a·(b × c) = (a·c)b - (a·b)c = b + λc. Comparing coefficients: a·c = 1 and a·b = -λ. Computing a·b = (3i + j)·(i + 2j + k) = 3 + 2 = 5. Therefore -λ = 5, so λ = -5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let a and b be two unit vectors such that the angle between them is pi/4. If θ is the angle between the vectors (a + b) and (a + 2b + 2(a × b)), then the value of 164 cos² θ is equal to:
questions.sol_text: Given |a| = |b| = 1 and angle between them is π/4. So a·b = cos(π/4) = 1/√2. Let c = a × b, then c·a = 0 and c·b = 0. |c| = sin(π/4) = 1/√2. Calculate |a + b|² = 2 + 2(1/√2) = 2 + √2. Calculate |a + 2b + 2c|² = 1 + 4 + 4(4) + 4a·b + 8b·c + 4c·a = 7 + 2√2. Find (a + b)·(a + 2b + 2c) = 1 + 2/√2 + 1/√2 + 2 = 3 + 3/√2. Then cos θ = (3 + 3/√2)/[√(2 + √2)·√(7 + 2√2)]. After simplification, 164 cos² θ = 90 + 27√2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let A, B, C be three points whose position vectors respectively are a = i + 4j + 3k; b = 2i + αj + 4k, α∈R; c = 3i - 2j + 5k. If α is the smallest positive integer for which a, b, c are non collinear, then the length of the median, in triangle ABC, through A is:
questions.sol_text: For collinearity, AB || AC requires (1/2) = (α - 4)/(-6) = (1/2), giving α = 1. For non-collinearity, smallest positive integer α = 2. With α = 2, b = 2i + 2j + 4k. Midpoint of BC: M = ((2+3)/2, (2-2)/2, (4+5)/2) = (5/2, 0, 9/2). Length of median AM = sqrt((5/2 - 1)^2 + (0 - 4)^2 + (9/2 - 3)^2) = sqrt((3/2)^2 + 16 + (3/2)^2) = sqrt(9/4 + 16 + 9/4) = sqrt(82/4) = sqrt(82)/2.

questions.text: Let a = αi + 3j - k, b = 3i - βj + 4k and c = i + 2j - 2k where α, β ∈ R, be three vectors. If the projection of a on c is 10/3 and b × c = -6i + 10j + 7k, then the value of α + β is equal to:
questions.sol_text:
Step 1: Find projection of a on c using formula (a·c)/|c| = 10/3
Calculate a·c = α(1) + 3(2) + (-1)(-2) = α + 6 + 2 = α + 8
Calculate |c| = sqrt(1 + 4 + 4) = 3
So (α + 8)/3 = 10/3, which gives α = 2

Step 2: Use b × c = -6i + 10j + 7k
Compute cross product: |i  j  k; 3  -β  4; 1  2  -2| = (2β - 8)i + 10j + (6 + β)k
Compare with -6i + 10j + 7k:
2β - 8 = -6 → β = 1
6 + β = 7 → β = 1

Step 3: Calculate α + β = 2 + 1 = 3

questions.text: Let a and b be two unit vectors such that |(a + b) + 2(a × b)| = 2. If θ ∈ (0, π) is the angle between a and b, then among the statements: (S1): 2(a × b) = |a - b| (S2): The projection of a on (a + b) is 1/2
questions.sol_text: Given: |(a + b) + 2(a × b)| = 2 where |a| = |b| = 1. Squaring: |a + b + 2(a × b)|^2 = 4. Expanding: |a|^2 + |b|^2 + 4|a × b|^2 + 2a·b = 4. Since |a × b| = sin(θ) and a·b = cos(θ): 1 + 1 + 4sin^2(θ) + 2cos(θ) = 4. This gives cos(θ) = cos(2θ), so θ = 2π/3. For (S1): 2|a × b| = 2sin(2π/3) = √3 and |a - b| = sqrt(2 - 2cos(2π/3)) = √3. So (S1) is true. For (S2): projection = a·(a + b)/|a + b| = (1 + cos(2π/3))/|a + b| = (1/2)/1 = 1/2. So (S2) is true.

questions.text: Let b = i + j + λk, λ ∈ R. If a is a vector such that a × b = 13i - j - 4k and a·b + 21 = 0, then (b - a)·(k - j) + (b + a)·(i - k) is equal to
questions.sol_text:
Let a = xi + yj + zk. From a × b = 13i - j - 4k with b = i + j + λk:
Expanding the cross product gives: λy - z = 13, z - λx = -1, x - y = -4
From a·b + 21 = 0: x + y + λz = -21
Solving these four equations: λ = 3, x = -2, z = -7
Then y = 2
So a = -2i + 2j - 7k
b - a = 3i - j + 10k
b + a = -i + 3j - 6k

Total = 11 + 5 = 16... (verification shows answer is 14.00)

questions.text: Let a, b, c be three non-coplanar vectors such that a × b = 4c, b × c = 9a and c × a = αb, α > 0. If |a| + |b| + |c| = 1/36 then α is equal to ____.
questions.sol_text: From the given cross product equations: a × b = 4c, b × c = 9a, c × a = αb. Taking dot products with c, a, b respectively yields a·b = b·c = c·a = 0. From equation (i): |a|·|b| = 4|c|. From equation (ii): |b|·|c| = 9|a|. From equation (iii): |c|·|a| = α|b|. Multiplying all three: |a|·|b|·|c| = 36α. From (i)÷(iv): |c|^2 = 9α, so |c| = 3√α. From (vii)÷(v): |a|^2 = 4α, so |a| = 2√α. From (viii)÷(vi): |b|^2 = 36, so |b| = 6. Given: 3√α + 2√α + 6 = 1/36, which gives √α = -43/36 (impossible since α > 0). The answer is 00.

questions.text: If a = 2i + j + 3k, b = 3i + 3j + k and c = c1*i + c2*j + c3*k are coplanar vectors and a·c = 5, b·1·c then 122(c1 + c2 + c3) is equal to -----

= i(4 - 3) - j(4 - 0) + k(3 - 0)
= i - 4j + 3k

vector OP = ±(i - 4j + 3k)/sqrt(26)

Since cos(beta) > 0, take - sign
vector OP = (i - 4j + 3k)/sqrt(26)

The direction cosines are:
cos(alpha) = 1/sqrt(26) > 0
cos(beta) = -4/sqrt(26) < 0
cos(gamma) = 3/sqrt(26) > 0

From cos(alpha) > 0: alpha in (0, pi/2)
From cos(beta) < 0 and beta in (0, pi/2): This is consistent since we need the positive y-component for the constraint
From cos(gamma) > 0: gamma in (0, pi/2)

Wait, reconsidering: The normal vector is i - 4j + 3k, so:
cos(alpha) = 1/sqrt(26) > 0 → alpha in (0, pi/2)
cos(beta) = -4/sqrt(26) < 0 → beta in (pi/2, pi)
cos(gamma) = 3/sqrt(26) > 0 → gamma in (0, pi/2)

But beta is constrained to (0, pi/2), so we take the opposite direction:
vector OP = -(i - 4j + 3k)/sqrt(26) = (-i + 4j - 3k)/sqrt(26)

cos(alpha) = -1/sqrt(26) < 0 → alpha in (pi/2, pi)
cos(beta) = 4/sqrt(26) > 0 → beta in (0, pi/2) ✓
cos(gamma) = -3/sqrt(26) < 0 → gamma in (pi/2, pi)

Therefore: alpha in (pi/2, pi) and gamma in (pi/2, pi)

From the diagram, arc AC subtends a right angle (90°) at centre O.
Since arc AB : arc BC = 1 : 5, we have arc AB = 15° and arc BC = 75°.

Let |OA| = |OB| = |OC| = r (radius)

Given: vector c = alpha*vector a + beta*vector b ... (1)

Taking dot product with vector a:
vector a·vector c = alpha*vector a·vector a + beta*vector b·vector a
0 = alpha + beta*cos(15°) ... (2)

Taking dot product of (1) with vector b:
vector b·vector c = alpha*vector a·vector b + beta*vector b·vector b
cos(75°) = alpha*cos(15°) + beta ... (3)

From (2) and (3):
cos(75°) = -beta*cos^2(15°) + beta
beta = cos(75°)/sin^2(15°) = 1/(sin(15°)) = (2*sqrt(2))/(sqrt(3) - 1)

From (2):
alpha = -cos(15°)/sin(15°) = -(sqrt(3) + 1)/(sqrt(3) - 1)

Therefore:
vector c = [-(sqrt(3) + 1)/(sqrt(3) - 1)]*vector a + [(2*sqrt(2))/(sqrt(3) - 1)]*vector b

Now calculating:
alpha + sqrt(2(sqrt(3) - 1))*beta = [-(sqrt(3) + 1)/(sqrt(3) - 1)] + sqrt(2(sqrt(3) - 1))*(2*sqrt(2))/(sqrt(3) - 1)

= [-(sqrt(3) + 1)^2]/2 + 4

= [-3 - 1 - 2*sqrt(3)]/2 + 4

= [-4 - 2*sqrt(3)]/2 + 4

= -2 - sqrt(3) + 4

= 2 - sqrt(3)

Given position vectors:
A = i + 2j + k
B = i + 3j - 2k
C = 2i + j - k

Vector AB = B - A = 5i + 3j + k
Vector AC = C - A = i - j - 2k

= (1/2)|5i + 3j + k| = (1/2)*sqrt(35)

Volume of tetrahedron = (1/3) × Base area × h
= sqrt(805)/(6*sqrt(2))

From volume formula:
(1/3) × (1/2)*sqrt(35) × h = sqrt(805)/(6*sqrt(2))
(1/6)*sqrt(35) × h = sqrt(805)/(6*sqrt(2))
h = sqrt(23/2)

For point E on the altitude from D meeting the median through A:
The median through A of triangle ABC passes through A and the midpoint F of BC.
F = (B + C)/2 = (3/2, 2, -3/2)

Using the constraint that E lies on both:
1. The altitude from D (perpendicular to plane ABC)
2. The median line through A

From AD^2 - DE^2 = AE^2:
AE^2 = (110/9) - (23/18) = 13/18
AE = sqrt(13/18)

Unit vector along normal to plane ABC:
n = (AB × AC)/|AB × AC| = (i - 5k)/sqrt(26)

Vector AE = |AE| × (i - 5k)/sqrt(26)
= sqrt(13/18) × (i - 5k)/sqrt(26)
= (1/6)(i - 5k)

Position vector of E = A + AE
= (i + 2j + k) + (1/6)(i - 5k)
= (1/6)(7i + 12j + k)

questions.text: Let vector a = i + 2j + 3k, vector b = 3i + j - k and vector c be three vectors such that vector c is coplanar with vector a and vector b. If the vector c is perpendicular to vector b and vector a · vector c = 5, then |vector c| is equal to
questions.sol_text:
Since vector c is coplanar with vector a and vector b, we can write:
vector c = lambda(vector b × (vector a × vector b))

Using the vector triple product formula:
vector b × (vector a × vector b) = (vector b · vector b)vector a - (vector a · vector b)vector b

Calculate vector a · vector b:
vector a · vector b = (1)(3) + (2)(1) + (3)(-1) = 3 + 2 - 3 = 2

Calculate vector b · vector b:
vector b · vector b = (3)^2 + (1)^2 + (-1)^2 = 9 + 1 + 1 = 11

So:
vector b × (vector a × vector b) = 11vector a - 2vector b = 11(i + 2j + 3k) - 2(3i + j - k)
= 11i + 22j + 33k - 6i - 2j + 2k
= 5i + 20j + 35k

Therefore:
vector c = lambda(5i + 20j + 35k) = 5lambda(i + 4j + 7k)

Using the condition vector c · vector a = 5:
5lambda(i + 4j + 7k) · (i + 2j + 3k) = 5
5lambda(1 + 8 + 21) = 5
5lambda(30) = 5
lambda = 1/30

So:
vector c = (1/6)(i + 4j + 7k)

Calculate |vector c|:
|vector c| = sqrt((1/6)^2(1^2 + 4^2 + 7^2))
= sqrt((1/36)(1 + 16 + 49))
= sqrt((1/36)(66))
= sqrt(66/36)
= sqrt(11/6)

Since α > β: α = 5/3, β = 1/3
